Question: Three balls are randomly and independently tossed into bins numbered with the positive integers so that for each ball, the probability that it is tossed into bin \(i\) is \(2^{-i}\) for \(i=1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(\ldots.\) More than one ball is allowed in each bin. The probability that the balls end up evenly spaced in distinct bins is \(\dfrac{p}{q},\) where \(p\) and \(q\) are relatively prime positive integers. (For example, the balls are evenly spaced if they are tossed into bins \(3,\) \(17,\) and \(10.\)) What is \(p+q?\)
